result.summary: Implements core BIP352 (Silent Payments) cryptographic operations, address parsing, and transaction output derivation in common/bip352.{h,cpp} wrapping the libsecp256k1 silentpayments module. Defines chain parameters for silent payments address prefixes across all networks and provides helper methods to extract public keys from inputs, generate destinations, and scan outputs using `SilentPaymentsReceiver`. Adds unit tests covering BIP352 test vectors for sending and receiving.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core cannot parse Silent Payments addresses, generate silent payment outputs, or scan transactions for silent payments. Integrating BIP352 directly into wallet code would entangle cryptographic routines and address formatting with wallet state and database mechanics.
evidence: Project tracking issue #28536 lays out the multi-stage roadmap for BIP352 integration in Bitcoin Core.
PR description notes this is 'the second iteration of #28122, now based on secp256k1/pull/1765' and separates core BIP logic from wallet and transaction implementation details.

enables: Silent Payments wallet sending and receiving (#28536)
Silent Payments block indexing for light clients (#28536)

result.scope_notes: Adds large test data vectors (data/bip352_send_and_receive_vectors.json, +5729 lines) and new common module files without wiring the functionality into the wallet or RPC interfaces yet.
result.changed_since_previous: Rebased with minor interface refinements to the bip352 wrapper classes, including transparent comparisons for SilentPaymentsLabel and explicit deleted copy/move semantics for SilentPaymentsReceiver.
result.card: Implements core BIP352 (Silent Payments) address decoding and cryptographic primitives in common/bip352.{h,cpp} backed by libsecp256k1, along with official BIP test vectors. Bitcoin Core currently has no native Silent Payments capabilities, preventing users from receiving funds without public address reuse. This PR establishes the isolated library layer necessary for subsequent wallet integration (sending, scanning, change management) and node-level indexing for light clients (#28536).

risk.why: The new BIP352 cryptographic and address handling logic is self-contained in common and only exercised by unit tests, with no integration into active wallet, consensus, or RPC paths.
